1859-the-works-of-max-beerbohm:
Max Beerbohm's Works gathers his early essays and caricatures in prose, with a bibliography by John Lane, and shows the young Beerbohm already master of his manner. The pieces move through art, theatre, and society, with Greek tags transliterated for the reader and jokes that land softly.

One essay notes, with mock grandeur, that the least of a certain renaissance was the discovery of America, and that its keenest students of the exquisite were women. Beerbohm writes as a dandy with a conscience, amused by his age and fond of it. The collection is the best introduction to a wit who never raised his voice.
podcast-dannyjones-LG6WC3AdUHM:
Joe Redner, Tampa's famous strip club owner, joins Danny Jones for episode 37 of the KONCRETE podcast. Redner built an empire of neon in Florida and fought city hall for decades over free speech. His clubs and his court battles made him a local legend.

Redner tells the story of his fights under the First Amendment, which he treats as a personal creed. He recounts arrests, lawsuits, and the politics of vice in a Southern city. Jones asks what keeps him fighting after so many years. Bold and free-minded listeners get a Florida original in full voice.
podcast-dannyjones-_6lhNwA-DhM:
Comedian Sam Tripoli joins Danny Jones to warn that the full Epstein files would shake the country to its base. The episode title puts his claim in strong words: the real files will destroy society. Tripoli mixes comedy with dark research.

Tripoli lays out what he thinks the unreleased files hold and who he thinks they would expose. Jones lets him build the case at full length, then asks what proof can be shown. The talk ranges over power, blackmail, and why so much stays sealed. The library holds the episode as an archive record, and listeners can judge the claims on their own.
the-olden-time-series-vol-5-some-strange: Some Strange and Curious Punishments is volume 5 of the Olden Time Series prepared by Henry M. Brooks of Salem, sold by Ticknor and Company of Boston at 50 cents a volume. Only the publisher's series pages and the title page are present here, so the punishment pieces themselves do not appear. The same series pages open the other Olden Time volumes in this group. Brooks drew his material chiefly from old newspapers of Boston and Salem.
the-works-of-max-beerbohm: The Works of Max Beerbohm appears here through notes and a contents list, without the essays themselves. A bibliography by John Lane accompanies the volume. The transcriber explains several Greek phrases used in the text. Contents include Dandies and Dandies and The Pervasion of Rouge. King George the Fourth and a piece called 1880 are also listed. Poor Romeo and Diminuendo close the list before the bibliography.
